proposal.utterance: What kind of BFO entity is the disposition to recognize authority?

entities.label: DispositionToRecognizeAuthority
entities.rationale: The disposition to recognize authority is an internally grounded realizable entity: it is borne by agents (persons, officials, institutions) and manifests when those bearers engage in acts of recognition or deference to authority. BFO_0000016 (Disposition) captures capacities that are grounded in the intrinsic nature of their bearer and that are realized in processes. This distinguishes it from a Role (BFO_0000023), which is externally grounded by social context, and from a Quality (BFO_0000019), which is not realizable. The existing class ActorWill (BFO_0000016) is related but denotes volitional capacity generally; DispositionToRecognizeAuthority is more specific and targets the normative-recognition capacity relevant to legal theory.

relations.rationale: Disposition to recognize authority is a subclass of BFO Disposition, inheriting the internally-grounded, realizable character.

open_questions: Should DispositionToRecognizeAuthority be modeled as a subclass of the existing working:ActorWill (also BFO_0000016), given ActorWill captures volitional/conative capacity? Or should they remain sibling subclasses of BFO_0000016?

Is the bearer of this disposition intended to be individual human agents (officials), collective agents (institutions), or both? This affects whether we need separate subclasses or a single class with different bearer ranges.
Should this disposition be linked to the existing working:CourtAuthority (BFO_0000023) as the authority-role that gets recognized when this disposition is realized?
proposal.rationale_summary: The disposition to recognize authority fits BFO_0000016 (Disposition) because it is an intrinsically grounded, realizable capacity inhering in an agent — it pre-exists any particular act of recognition and is realized in processes of acknowledgment (cf. working:ActOfAcknowledgment, BFO_0000015). It is not a Role (BFO_0000023) because roles are externally conferred by social context rather than grounded in the bearer's own nature; and it is not merely a Quality (BFO_0000019) because it has the further structure of being realizable in behavior. The proposal mints a new class working:DispositionToRecognizeAuthority as a subclass of BFO_0000016, keeping it distinct from the existing working:ActorWill while remaining in the same BFO category. The open questions flag key modeling decisions the user should resolve before commitment.
